title: What she hath done (Mark 14:1–11)
hook: the anointing at Bethany: what she did will be told wherever the gospel is preached

segments.voice: Yesterday, one word from the Mount of Olives: watch. Your line was watch. When did you catch yourself on autopilot? Today the passion begins, with a woman who was wide awake. Day two hundred twenty-five.

It's two days before Passover. In Jerusalem, the chief priests and scribes are looking for a quiet way to arrest Jesus and put him to death. Not during the feast, they say, or the people will riot. Meanwhile, just over the hill in the village of Bethany, Jesus is at dinner in the house of a man called Simon the leper. A woman walks in holding an alabaster jar of perfume, pure nard, very expensive. She doesn't open it. She breaks it. And she pours the whole thing over his head. The room fills with the smell, and with outrage.
screen: `TWO DAYS BEFORE PASSOVER.` → `A DINNER IN BETHANY.` → `SHE BREAKS THE JAR.`

segments.voice: First, the complaint. Some at the table are indignant. What a waste. That could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii, close to a year's wages for a laborer, and given to the poor. It sounds reasonable. It sounds even holy. Second, Jesus defends her. In the Douay-Rheims: "Let her alone, why do you molest her? She hath wrought a good work upon me." You'll always have the poor with you, he says, and you can do them good whenever you want. You won't always have me. Then: "She hath done what she could: she is come beforehand to anoint my body for the burial." She seems to understand what the disciples still don't: he's going to die. Third, the anointing itself. Remember, Christ means the anointed one. Kings were anointed on the head. Here, in a friend's house, a woman whose name Mark never tells us anoints the king. Not a priest. Not an apostle. Her. Fourth, the promise: "wheresoever this gospel shall be preached in the whole world, that also which she hath done, shall be told for a memory of her." And it has been, in every language the Gospel reached, including right now, in your ears. Then look what Mark puts right next to her. Judas, one of the twelve, goes to the chief priests to hand Jesus over, and they promise him money. She's unnamed and remembered forever for pouring out something precious. He's named, and he's selling someone precious. John's Gospel tells a similar anointing and names the woman Mary of Bethany. Mark lets her stay nameless, and remembered anyway.
screen: `WHAT A WASTE, THEY SAY.` · `LET HER ALONE: A GOOD WORK.` · `SHE ANOINTS THE ANOINTED ONE.` · `TOLD WHEREVER THE GOSPEL GOES.` · then, large: `SHE HATH DONE WHAT SHE COULD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: tell someone's kindness to another. Settle and breathe. Think of someone who did something good that nobody noticed. A coworker who covered for you. A neighbor who shoveled your walk. A grandparent who quietly held a family together. Let their face come to mind, and remember exactly what they did. Now decide who you'll tell about it today, so it's told for a memory of them. If you pray, you can thank God for them by name. The bell holds the time.
What she hath done. The woman at Bethany who broke the jar and anointed Jesus, and the promise that it would be told wherever the gospel goes. Today's word.
Your line: she did what she could. Today, do the one generous thing in front of you, even if someone calls it a waste. Day two hundred twenty-five.

howItsDone: The Church reads the anointing at Bethany during Holy Week, and Catholic bishops bless the holy oils at the Chrism Mass that same week, the oils used for anointing at baptism, confirmation, ordination and for the sick.

original.note: Greek: a memorial, a remembrance. told for a memory of her.

trapdoor: what you thought: a woman wasted expensive perfume.
what it means: she anoints the anointed one for burial, understanding what the disciples don't, and is remembered forever.
what a scholar hears: a Markan sandwich, the plot, the anointing, Judas: an unnamed woman's gift framed by a named man's betrayal.

notes: Douay-Rheims Mark 14:6, 14:8, 14:9 given from memory; confirm wording.
'Three hundred pence' (denarii) as 'close to a year's wages', based on a denarius as a day's wage (Matthew 20:2): confirm.
Mary of Bethany is named only in John's parallel; the Western tradition that merged her with Mary Magdalene and the woman of Luke 7 is not raised. Keeper may wish to add or keep out.
Anointing of the head read as royal/messianic: common commentary reading; confirm framing.
Chrism Mass during Holy Week in howItsDone: confirm.
